audience.role: Plugin users, 0.7.0 upgraders, and maintainers evaluating host/Node floors, the cancellation semantics change and dependency risk

checks.note: READMEs explain fit, floors and first use; changelogs record the 0.7.0-to-0.8.0 delta; the release draft frames the upgrade decision; the security policy carries the risk record; the acceptance record scopes evidence and pending gates.

Upgrader paraphrase: before installing 0.8.0, upgrade DSH to >=0.2.2-rc.1 and Node to >=24.9.0; older hosts are refused, no old-API fallback. 0.7.0-and-earlier semantic runs no longer resume (finish with the creating version or start anew); old caches invalidate automatically; existing reports stay readable. Install via registry once 0.8.0 is published, else a reviewed tarball/source revision; --deterministic skips the model stage.

Caller cancellation is introduced through its concrete effect (a settled outcome counted separately, side effects still possible) before the error-code names; ABORTED / ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH and their error.code/info.code locations are explained locally; the input-identity term is tied to the observable resume refusal.

Candidate state is explicit everywhere (unpublished, registry command gated on publication); source/interface results are separated from pending exact-commit CI, native dual-platform acceptance, artifact freeze, publication and consumer adoption; local scan results are marked as not exact-commit CI; range admission is not claimed as future-host testing; historical 0.2.1-rc.2 vocabulary statements stay in provenance position.

Each README opens with purpose and first command, states floors and upgrade actions in the install section, and moves mechanism detail (cancellation taxonomy, recovery, PTC, generations) into later reference sections; the release draft leads with the floor decision before the risk and limits sections.

All three READMEs and both changelogs state the same floors, resume contract, cancellation semantics, known-gap decision and install commands independently in their own language; the bilingual release draft carries both editions in one file with matching facts.

findings.message: Bundled release-candidate auditor advisories carried over from 0.7.0: install command appears after the first 50 lines, exact-version compatibility claims need provenance classification (current spec versus historical statements are already separated in the compatibility section), and a Russian changelog edition does not exist. None blocks comprehension.

limitations: This receipt binds reader comprehension of the listed bytes only; it does not establish factual correctness beyond the recorded evidence, native acceptance, exact-commit CI, publication or human preference.
The candidate is unpublished: README registry commands describe a future published state and are marked as such; readers testing the candidate must use a reviewed tarball or source revision.
A Russian changelog edition remains a coverage gap carried over from 0.7.0; the Russian README is independently readable and links the English changelog.
